verdict.summary: You create a public connection in Notion's Developer portal and get a client ID and secret straight away. If you set installation scope to 'Any workspace', any Notion user can install it through OAuth with no review. Notion only reviews Marketplace listings (a security review plus a listing review), and listing is optional. The main trap is that installation scope is permanent once the connection is created.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min (add 1-3 hours if you want a Marketplace listing)
verdict.approval_wait: none for OAuth installs; 5-10 business days for a listing response if you choose to list on the Marketplace (Notion gives no timeline for the security review)

gates.name: Public connection in your development workspace
gates.unlocks: You can complete OAuth with your own Notion account and share pages from your development workspace with the connection.
limits: Rate limit per connection: 600 requests/min on Business and Enterprise workspaces, 180/min on other plans, plus a shared per-workspace limit
Users only see pages they have full access to in the page picker

gates.name: Selected workspaces only, or an unlisted 'Any workspace' connection
gates.unlocks: Invited users can install the connection through your OAuth link. 'Selected workspaces only' limits installs to workspaces you choose. An unlisted 'Any workspace' connection works for anyone who has the link.
limits: Notion documents no install cap or user cap for unlisted connections
You cannot change installation scope after creating the connection, and 'Selected workspaces only' connections can never be listed on the Marketplace
On Enterprise plans, workspace owners can restrict which connections members may install

gates.name: 'Any workspace' public connection (optionally listed on the Marketplace)
gates.unlocks: Any Notion user in any workspace can install the connection through OAuth, with no review. A Marketplace listing adds discoverability and requires Notion's security review and listing review.
limits: A Marketplace listing requires Notion's security review and a listing review
Notion says to expect a listing response within 5-10 business days by email, and gives no timeline for the security review
Enterprise workspace owners may block installs that aren't on their approved list
gates.time_to_reach: Immediate for OAuth installs; listing response in 5-10 business days

steps.title: Open the Notion Developer portal
steps.detail: Sign in to Notion and go to app.notion.com/developers. Since the May 13, 2026 release, any workspace member can build connections, not only workspace owners.
gotchas: Older third-party guides point to notion.so/my-integrations and an Internal-to-Public toggle. The current flow is Build > Public connections in the Developer portal.
Notion doesn't say which workspace plan, if any, is required to create a public connection.

steps.title: Start a new public connection
steps.detail: In the Build section, open Public connections and click Create new connection. Enter a Connection name and choose your development workspace.
gotchas: Create a public connection, not an internal connection or a personal access token. Only public connections use OAuth.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI
steps.detail: In the redirect URI field of the same form, paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config. Notion requires the redirect_uri sent in the OAuth request to match a URI configured on the connection.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Use an absolute URL with no fragments or wildcards (from community guidance).
Composio has used more than one callback URL. Copy the one your Composio project shows.

steps.title: Choose installation scope: Any workspace
steps.detail: Pick 'Any workspace' if anyone outside your chosen workspaces will ever install the connection, or if you might list it on the Marketplace later. Pick 'Selected workspaces only' only for an internal or private tool.
gotchas: You cannot change installation scope after creation. A wrong choice means deleting the connection and creating a new one, which gives you a new client ID and secret.

steps.title: Select capabilities
steps.detail: Turn on only the capabilities your agent needs: Read content, Update content, Insert content, and a user-information level (none, names without email, or names with email). These capabilities take the place of OAuth scopes, so leave scopes empty in Composio.
gotchas: Turn on user information with email addresses only if you need it. It exposes users' emails and you'll have to justify it in a Marketplace review.

steps.title: Copy the OAuth client ID and secret
steps.detail: Open the connection's Configuration tab and copy the OAuth client ID, OAuth client secret and authorization URL. Store the secret in a secrets manager.
gotchas: Check the tab names when you get there. Notion's docs say they may differ slightly as the portal changes.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config with your credentials
steps.detail: In Composio, create a custom OAuth2 auth config for the notion toolkit and paste in your client ID and secret. The endpoints are https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize and https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token, and the token endpoint uses HTTP Basic auth with your client ID and secret.
gotchas: The authorize request must include response_type=code and owner=user.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection through Composio, approve it in Notion's page picker, and share at least one page. Then call the API, for example a search or a page read, to confirm the token works.
gotchas: Notion doesn't reject a wrong client_id at the authorize step: the page loads normally. If the flow fails later, check the client ID first.
The page picker shows only pages the user has full access to. An empty picker usually means the user lacks permissions.

steps.title: Check that token refresh stores the new refresh token
steps.detail: Force a token refresh and confirm the new refresh token replaces the old one. Every Notion refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token.
gotchas: Notion doesn't document the access token lifetime. Refresh when a request returns 401 instead of relying on expires_in.

steps.title: Share the connection and watch its health
steps.detail: Send other users your Composio connect link. An 'Any workspace' connection needs no review for this. Check the connection's Health tab in the Developer portal for failed requests, rate-limiting and blocked-request warnings.
gotchas: Enterprise workspaces may require an owner to approve your connection before members can install it.
A public_api_request_blocked error means Notion has restricted the connection. Retrying won't help, so contact Notion support.

steps.title: (Optional) Draft a Marketplace listing
steps.detail: In the Developer portal under Listings > Connections, click 'Start a new connection listing' under Drafts. Fill in name, description, category, tags, images and logo, then select your public connection.
gotchas: Notion rejects listings for brand or trademark problems and for quality concerns. Don't use Notion's marks in a way that implies endorsement.

steps.title: (Optional) Submit the listing for review
steps.detail: Submit the listing from the Connections page. A connection must pass Notion's security review before it can appear on the Marketplace.

steps.title: (Optional) Wait for Notion's decision
steps.detail: Notion says to expect an email within 5-10 business days. If changes are needed, Notion sends feedback and you can resubmit. Your OAuth connection keeps working for users during the review.

requirements.detail: The redirect_uri in the authorize request must match a URI configured on the connection. You must also send redirect_uri in the code exchange when more than one is configured.

requirements.item: HTTP Basic auth on the token endpoint
requirements.detail: The code exchange and refresh calls authenticate with the client ID and secret using HTTP Basic auth.
Each refresh returns a new refresh token, which must replace the stored one.
Required for installs outside workspaces you select and for Marketplace eligibility. You can't change it after creation.
Required before a listing appears on the Marketplace. It is not required for OAuth installs.
Name, description, category, tags, images and logo for the Marketplace listing draft.

scopes.effect: Lets the connection read pages and databases the user shared. Notion has published no sensitivity tiers.
Lets the connection edit existing content. It's set in the connection's capabilities, not as an OAuth scope.
Lets the connection create new content. It's set in the connection's capabilities.
Returns user names but not email addresses.
Adds email addresses to user objects. It affects user privacy, so expect to justify it in a Marketplace review.

blockers.symptom: Users outside your chosen workspaces can't install the connection, or the Marketplace listing option is unavailable
blockers.cause: The connection was created with 'Selected workspaces only', and installation scope can't be changed later.
blockers.fix: Create a new public connection with 'Any workspace' and update your client ID and secret in Composio.

blockers.symptom: OAuth fails at redirect or during the token exchange
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri doesn't match the one configured on the connection, or wasn't sent with the code exchange.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL into the connection's redirect URIs and make sure the code exchange sends it.

blockers.symptom: Users get logged out after their first token refresh
blockers.cause: The old refresh token was reused. Notion rotates the refresh token on every refresh.
blockers.fix: Store the new refresh token returned by every refresh.

blockers.symptom: A rejection email for the Marketplace listing
blockers.cause: Brand or trademark problems, quality concerns, or the connection doesn't meet Notion's baseline criteria.
blockers.fix: Address the feedback in the email and resubmit. Your OAuth installs keep working in the meantime.

blockers.symptom: API calls return the rate-limit reason public_api_request_blocked
blockers.cause: Notion has restricted the connection's API access.
blockers.fix: Stop retrying and contact Notion support. Use the Health tab to see what triggered it.

blockers.symptom: Enterprise users can't install the connection
blockers.cause: Their workspace owner limits installs to approved connections.
blockers.fix: Ask the workspace owner to add your connection to the approved list.

composio.note: Composio's managed Notion OAuth app works for prototyping. Notion uses capabilities rather than scopes, so no scopes are needed. Register your own public connection when you want your own name and logo on the consent screen, your own redirect URI, control over capabilities and rate limits, or a Marketplace listing. Your own 'Any workspace' connection can be installed by anyone without review, so switching to it doesn't put you in a review queue. Only a Marketplace listing needs Notion's review, and managed auth doesn't get you past that.

evidence.claim: Public connections are created in the Notion Developer portal. The Build section's Public connections page has a Create new connection form that asks for a connection name, development workspace, redirect URI(s), installation scope, and capabilities.
evidence.quote: Click Create new connection and fill in the required fields, including: Connection name and development workspace

evidence.claim: Notion says to expect a response within 5-10 business days after submitting a listing. It does not give a stated timeline for the separate security review.
evidence.quote: expect to hear back from our team within 5-10 business days via email.

evidence.claim: Notion says connections can be rejected for reasons ranging from brand or trademark problems to quality concerns, or when baseline connection criteria are not met. A rejected applicant gets an email explaining why and can resubmit.
evidence.quote: Connections are rejected for various reasons, from brand/trademark issues to quality concerns

evidence.claim: Notion's OAuth flow sends users to api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, and owner=user. The redirect_uri must match the one set on the connection in the Developer portal.
evidence.quote: Always use code. | owner | Always use user.

evidence.claim: Users choose which pages to share with the connection in a page picker. The picker only shows pages the user has full access to.
evidence.quote: The page picker only displays pages or databases to which a user has full access

evidence.claim: Notion's token endpoint is https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token. Code exchange and refresh both use HTTP Basic auth built from the client ID and secret, and the redirect_uri must be sent with the code exchange (it is required when more than one redirect URI is configured).
evidence.quote: The request is authorized using HTTP Basic Authentication.

evidence.claim: Notion issues a refresh_token alongside the access_token. Refreshing returns a new access token and a new refresh token, so the stored refresh token must be replaced after every refresh.
evidence.quote: Refreshing an access token will generate a new access token and a new refresh token.

evidence.claim: The Notion authorization docs do not mention PKCE. They also do not state an access token lifetime (expires_in) in the sections I read.
Notion uses capabilities, not OAuth scopes. Capabilities include Read content, Update content, Insert content, and user information (none, names without email, or with email addresses).
evidence.quote: No user information: Selecting this option prevents a connection from requesting any information about users.

evidence.claim: Email access is a separate user-information capability choice. Selecting user information with email addresses returns email in user objects, so it is a narrower-or-broader choice to justify at review. Notion has not published a sensitive or restricted capability list that I could find.

Rate limits apply per connection, by workspace plan: 600 requests per minute on Business and Enterprise, and 180 per minute on other plans. There is also a separate shared limit per workspace across all connections.
evidence.quote: Business and Enterprise | 600 requests per minute (an average of 10 per second)

evidence.claim: After creating the connection, the Configuration tab of the Developer portal shows the OAuth client ID and client secret, which the token exchange needs.
evidence.quote: visit the Configuration tab to retrieve your OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret.

evidence.claim: The official request-limits page lists no approval-based boost for public connections, and no unreviewed-app install cap. Some third-party blogs say 3 req/s applies until review, and that 100 req/s can be requested. I could not confirm either from Notion's own docs.
Any Notion user can install a public connection with 'Any workspace' scope. On Enterprise plans, workspace owners can restrict which connections members may install and maintain an approved list.
evidence.quote: On Enterprise plans, workspace owners can limit which connections members are allowed to install.

evidence.claim: Since the May 13, 2026 release, any Notion member (not only workspace owners) can build connections. Workspace-scoped OAuth and personal access tokens were added as well.
evidence.quote: Any member can build connections (not just Workspace Owners).

evidence.claim: The October 26, 2026 Notion Developers update added a Health tab in the Developer portal for internal and public connections. It shows the last 24 hours of API requests, failures and reasons, and warns about blocked requests and high client-error or rate-limit rates.
evidence.quote: Internal and public connections now have a Health tab in the Developer portal.
flags: cited URL was not retrieved during this research run

evidence.claim: Notion's public-connection docs show a 'Connection health' feature in the Developer portal and a 'public_api_request_blocked' rate-limit reason, which means a connection's API access was restricted and retrying will not help.
evidence.quote: This connection's API access has been restricted. Retrying won't help. Contact Notion support.

evidence.claim: The OAuth authorize endpoint is live. A probe with an invalid client_id and a Composio callback redirected to app.notion.com/install-integration (a JS page) without an OAuth error parameter, so an invalid client is not rejected at the authorize step.

Third-party guides say a Notion OAuth app is created at notion.so/my-integrations, defaults to Internal, and must be switched to Public before a client ID and secret are shown. This is community guidance and predates the current portal.
evidence.quote: When creating a Notion OAuth app, it is set to Internal by default.

evidence.claim: Community guides say the redirect URI must have a protocol and cannot include fragments, relative paths, wildcards, or a public IP. This is from an older tutorial, not from current official docs.
evidence.quote: It can't contain URL fragments, relative paths or wildcards, and can't be a public IP.

evidence.claim: Notion's current pages describe public connections as a Developer portal flow, in a Build section, with the authorization URL shown on the Configuration tab. Verify the exact tab names when setting up.
evidence.quote: Find this URL in the Configuration tab of your connection in the Developer portal.

evidence.claim: Notion's developer docs say the Developer portal is at app.notion.com/developers, and it is live without a login wall in the probe (the page itself requires JavaScript).
Notion's Overview separates three connection types: internal connections, public connections (OAuth 2.0), and personal access tokens. Public connections are the path for installation by other users.
evidence.quote: Public connections use OAuth 2.0 for authentication.

evidence.claim: Installation scope is picked at creation time: either 'Any workspace' (any Notion user can install, Marketplace-eligible) or 'Selected workspaces only' (restricted to chosen workspaces, not Marketplace-eligible). It cannot be changed after creation.
evidence.quote: Any workspace | Any Notion user, in any workspace.

evidence.claim: Public connections must go through a Notion security review before they can be listed on the Marketplace. A public connection can be built and used through OAuth without being listed.
evidence.quote: Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Listing on the Marketplace is optional. Without a listing, a public connection still works through its OAuth flow.
evidence.quote: Listing on the Marketplace is optional and helps your connection reach a wider audience

evidence.claim: Marketplace listing is a separate step. You start a draft in the Listings > Connections dashboard, add name, description, category, tags, images and logo, and select the public connection to associate with it. You submit it for review from the Connections page.
evidence.quote: Under Drafts, click Start a new connection listing.

evidence.claim: The Notion team reviews every Marketplace listing submission. Approved listings appear in the Marketplace, and when changes are needed, Notion sends feedback and the listing can be resubmitted.
evidence.quote: The Notion team reviews every listing submission.

open_questions: Notion's official docs show no install cap or user limit for unlisted public connections.
Notion doesn't publish the security review's criteria or timeline. The 5-10 business days applies to the listing response only.
The Connection Gallery Best Practices guide, which may list baseline review criteria, wasn't reviewed.
Notion doesn't say which capabilities count as sensitive in review.
Composio has used more than one callback URL (v1 auth-apps/add and v3 toolkits/auth/callback). Use the one your project shows.
It's not confirmed whether a free workspace is enough to create a public connection.
Third-party blogs mention a lower rate limit before review and a higher limit on request. Notion's docs don't confirm either.
